description: Dashboard daily delivery throughput bar chart: one bar per trailing day (30) encoding completed with a stacked darker failed segment, a client-side 7-day moving average overlay, and loading/error/empty states. Purely additive read on the web against the existing daily completion metrics endpoint and the dashboard chart baseline — no server, event, or data-collection change.

tasks.title: Add SegmentedBarSeries primitive to the dashboard chart kit
tasks.description: Extend the pinned chart kit in packages/web/src/pages/dashboard/charts/ with a new SegmentedBarSeries primitive that renders one multi-segment bar per datum (here: completed as a light bottom-anchored segment and failed as a darker bottom-anchored segment at the same x/width), scaling every segment against a single caller-supplied max on one shared count axis. This is the chart-kit enabler for the two-tone bar; the existing BarSeries (used by CostTrendChart) stays untouched to keep baseline regression risk isolated, per design D2.
acceptanceCriteria: SegmentedBarSeries accepts per-bar ordered segments (value + fill token) and a caller-supplied max, and renders one bar per datum at the provided x positions/width.

Each segment is a bottom-anchored <rect> scaled by value/max using the existing transform: scaleY() + transformOrigin: bottom + useReducedMotion() motion pattern from BarSeries (transform-based, prefers-reduced-motion-aware).
A segment with value 0 renders a zero-height rect (not omitted), so a zero-completed day with failures still shows the failed segment.
All segments scale to the single caller-supplied max on one shared axis (no per-segment rescale, no dual axis).
Colors are sourced from theme tokens via the caller-provided fill per segment (no hardcoded hex).
No new charting library dependency is introduced; the primitive composes only with the existing chart kit.

Dedicated unit tests (e.g. SegmentedBarSeries.test.tsx) cover: multi-segment rendering, segment scaling to max, zero-value segment present, reduced-motion branch; npm run typecheck -w packages/web and the new tests pass.
The existing BarSeries and CostTrendChart are unchanged and their tests remain green.
tasks.notes: Design D1 (single shared count axis, not cumulative stacking) and D2 (new focused primitive, BarSeries untouched). The primitive is axis-max-agnostic: ThroughputChart (T-003) computes and passes max = max over days of max(completed, failed).

tasks.title: Add daily completion throughput hook and 7-day moving average helper
tasks.description: Provide the data + model layer for daily throughput. Refactor fetchCompletionTrend(projectId) to fetchCompletionTrend(projectId, bucket = 'week') so the weekly hook's signature, query key (['issues','metrics','completion','week', projectId]) and URL stay identical (existing weekly tests stay green). Add useCompletionThroughput() with query key ['issues','metrics','completion','day', projectId] calling fetchCompletionTrend(projectId, 'day') at staleTime 60_000, enabled !!projectId. Add a pure computeMovingAverage(values, window) helper (trailing, inclusive of the current day, partial window at the leading edge) in a new productivity/model module, per design D3/D4.
acceptanceCriteria: fetchCompletionTrend accepts a bucket argument defaulting to 'week' and threads it into both the request URL and the request path; the existing weekly call sites compile and behave unchanged.

useCompletionThroughput() uses query key ['issues','metrics','completion','day', projectId], calls fetchCompletionTrend(projectId, 'day'), and sets staleTime: 60_000 and enabled: !!projectId (mirrors useCompletionTrend).
The existing completion-trend.test.ts weekly contract (query key + URL) stays green without modification.
New hook tests assert the daily query key, the daily URL (bucket=day), enabled/staleTime behavior, and decoding of a dense 30-bucket response carrying per-bucket Completed and Failed.
computeMovingAverage(values: number[], window: number): number[] returns an array of the same length; sma[i] = sum(values[max(0,i-window+1)..i]) / (i - max(0,i-window+1) + 1) per design D4.

computeMovingAverage is pure (no IO) and unit-tested for: partial leading window (fewer than window-1 predecessors still plots, never null/gap), all-zero input, window > length, and single-element input.
No new DTO is introduced; the existing bucket-agnostic CompletionBucketPoint / CompletionTrendResponse types are reused.
npm run typecheck -w packages/web and the new/existing tests pass.
tasks.notes: Design D3 (parameterize fetch by bucket, daily hook alongside weekly, weekly contract untouched) and D4 (pure, unit-tested SMA helper). Input is the dense completed: number[] (server guarantees 30 buckets with zeros), so no null handling is needed and the resulting line is a single continuous segment. Independent of T-001 (data/math, no chart primitives).

tasks.title: Implement ThroughputChart widget and mount it in the Dashboard Productivity zone
tasks.description: Build the ThroughputChart widget that composes the SegmentedBarSeries primitive (T-001) and LineSeries with the daily hook + computeMovingAverage (T-002) into the visible feature: one bar per trailing day (completed in fill-chart-2 with a darker failed segment in fill-chart-4 on a single shared count axis), a 7-day moving average overlay (stroke-chart-5) computed client-side over completed only, and loading/error/empty states routed through the shared three-state wrapper. Mount it in ProductivityZone directly after CompletionTrend (design D7).
acceptanceCriteria: ThroughputChart renders one bar per trailing day across the fixed 30-day window; each bar's height encodes that day's completed count sourced from useCompletionThroughput, with a darker failed segment encoding the same bucket's Failed value.

Axis max = max over days of max(completed, failed); a day with completed=0 still renders a zero-height bar (not a gap) and, if it has failures, renders the failed segment (cumulative stacking is NOT used).

A 7-day moving average line is overlaid, computed client-side via computeMovingAverage over the completed counts only (failed is never folded in); MA renders even for leading days with fewer than six predecessors.

Per-day values are sourced exclusively from the existing completion metrics endpoint at bucket=day (bucketed by IssueWorkCompleted/IssueClosed terminal-event time); no new collection path and no client re-bucketing by updatedAt.

Loading state renders while data is in flight and error state renders on fetch failure, both via the shared ChartContainer three-state wrapper; chart content does not render until data resolves and no stale/fabricated content is shown.

Empty state (all buckets completed+failed === 0) renders via ChartContainer status='empty' with copy naming the next action ('Throughput appears once an issue completes on this project'); a bare empty axis is never rendered. Failure-only throughput is NOT empty (its failed bars render).

Accessibility wrapper exposes an SR data summary (window, peak day, total/average completed) and a ChartLegend with three entries (Completed bar / Failed bar / 7-day average line) disambiguated by label + shape (a non-color channel), satisfying the SHALL.
Theme-token colors (fill-chart-2, fill-chart-4, stroke-chart-5), tabular-nums, and transform-based prefers-reduced-motion-aware motion are used; no new charting library dependency is introduced.
The widget performs no domain write (read-only); it only reads the additive daily-resolution completion metrics endpoint.
<ThroughputChart/> is rendered in ProductivityZone directly after <CompletionTrend/>; ProductivityZone.test.tsx is updated to mock the widget and assert containment (existing mock/assert pattern).

Widget tests mirror CostTrendChart.test.tsx coverage: three-state rendering, bar completed/failed values from daily buckets, MA values, legend entries, empty-state next action, and theme-token color usage; npm run typecheck -w packages/web and npm run test:run -w packages/web pass.
tasks.output: packages/web/src/pages/dashboard/productivity/ThroughputChart.tsx (+ ThroughputChart.test.tsx); ThroughputChart mounted in ProductivityZone.tsx with ProductivityZone.test.tsx updated
tasks.notes: Composes T-001 (SegmentedBarSeries) and T-002 (useCompletionThroughput + computeMovingAverage). Design D1 (single shared count axis), D5 (color tokens + label/shape legend), D6 (window-scoped empty heuristic mirroring CostTrendChart hasUsageData), D7 (mount after CompletionTrend). Rollback = remove the single <ThroughputChart/> mount line; everything else is additive/opt-in and the fetchCompletionTrend signature change is backward-compatible (default arg).
